methodology.task: Frozen text-observation decision accuracy, not live task completion or screenshot performance.
methodology.ordering: Sequential requests; each observation is sent to every provider. Provider order rotates left one position each repetition.
methodology.latency: Successful request latency is the existing Akamai app server provider-adapter wall time returned by its API: network, provider routing where applicable, inference, response transfer and validation. Jupyter coordination and loopback client overhead are excluded. Failed API requests retain measured client wall time and are counted as incorrect. All 72 attempts included; no discarded warmup, retry, fallback, or local cache.
methodology.percentiles: Linear interpolation at sorted rank (n-1)*p; small N, descriptive only.
methodology.accuracy: All named choices must match ground truth; array ground truth accepts any listed choice. Request failures count as incorrect.
methodology.groundTruth: Only state and questions are passed to execute_decision. Expected answers are used after inference for scoring.
methodology.confidence: Native confidence and probabilities are preserved without calibration, thresholds, or transformations. Chat returns null confidence/probabilities.
methodology.clefRouting: cloudflare/clef-flash pinned to Cloudflare with provider.only and allow_fallbacks=false; no substituted models.
methodology.lunaRouting: openai/gpt-6-luna through OpenRouter Chat Completions, strict JSON schema, reasoning effort none.
limitations: Two observations per demo and three repetitions are not representative production coverage.
Repeated inputs may benefit from upstream prompt caches; no local result cache is used.
Frozen observations do not test model recovery from earlier mistakes or complete workflow success.
The GPU local-cluster route differs from hosted OpenRouter network routes. Request-wall-time differences include networking and provider routing, not only inference.
Earlier browser smoke calls warmed providers; no benchmark attempts were discarded, and upstream caching was not controlled.
methodology.network: All four providers were requested sequentially by the same existing Akamai application process during this benchmark. GPU uses its local cluster endpoint; Clef, JEV and Luna use external OpenRouter routes. Network routes still differ by provider, so this is not an inference-only speed comparison.
methodology.gpuRouting: Cloudflare/clef-flash served by self-hosted Akamai GPU; no provider router or model substitution.
methodology.command: python scripts/benchmark_providers.py --providers gpu clef jev luna --repeats 3 --fixtures evidence/frozen-observations.json --output akamai-frozen-benchmark.json (execute_decision delegated to the existing local app API; server-measured latencies retained)
methodology.annotation: Exact frozen CLI scoring and ordering retained. Private deployment URLs and nonessential request IDs are excluded from public evidence. Credential files were not read by this benchmark; the existing configured app made the provider calls.
